rules.title: Off-road diesel rule covers vehicles of 25 hp or more
rules.plain_english: CARB's off-road diesel fleet rule applies to anyone who owns or operates in California a self-propelled off-road diesel vehicle (excavator, loader, dozer, backhoe, crane, forklift and the like) with an engine of 25 horsepower or more, including rented and leased machines. Two-engine cranes, drill rigs and similar vehicles with a 50 bhp or larger auxiliary engine are also covered.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Except as provided in subsection (b)(2) below, this regulation applies to any person, business, or government agency who owns or operates within California any vehicles with a diesel-fueled or alternative diesel fueled off-road compression-ignition engine with maximum power (max hp) of 25 horsepower (hp) or greater provided that the vehicle cannot be registered and driven safely on-road or was not designed to be driven on-road, even if it has been modified so that it can be driven safely on-road.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's 15-Day Modified Text (Attachment A-1, released April 10, 2023) with the struck 15-day deletions removed. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The adopting executive order (reported in search excerpts as R-23-001) and the FSOR returned CARB's rate-limit page (HTTP 419), so the final order was not read; any post-15-day nonsubstantive edits are not reflected. Exempt: vehicles used solely for agriculture, personal-use vehicles, vehicles awaiting sale (2449(e)(10)-(11)); emergency-only, snow-removal and over-half-agricultural vehicles still report and label.

rules.title: Off-road fleet size: small up to 2,500 hp, medium 2,501-5,000 hp, large over 5,000 hp
rules.plain_english: Fleet size is set by adding the horsepower of every off-road diesel vehicle under common ownership or control. Over 5,000 hp is a large fleet, 2,500 hp or less is a small fleet, and anything in between is medium. All state and federal government fleets count as large, whatever their size.

rules.verbatim_quote: “Large fleet” – A fleet with a total max hp (as defined below) greater than 5,000 hp. [...] (B) “Medium fleet” – A fleet that is not a small or large fleet. (C) “Small fleet” – A fleet with total max hp of less than or equal to 2,500 hp that is owned by a business, non-profit organization, or local municipality, a local municipality fleet in a low population county irrespective of total max hp, a non-profit training center irrespective of total max hp, or a captive attainment area fleet irrespective of total max hp.

rules.title: Low-use, snow-removal and emergency-only vehicles are left out of fleet horsepower

rules.verbatim_quote: “Total maximum power” (total max hp) means the sum of the max hp for all of a fleet’s engines that are subject to this regulation. Permanent and year-by-year low-use vehicles, dedicated snow-removal vehicles, and vehicles used solely for emergency operations shall not be included in the sum.

rules.title: Fleet includes every company under the same owners or managers
rules.plain_english: Vehicles owned by different companies still count as one fleet if the same people manage them day to day, or the same majority stockholders control the companies. You cannot split equipment into separate LLCs to stay a small fleet.

Vehicles managed by the same directors, officers, or managers, or by corporations controlled by the same majority stockholders are considered to be under common ownership or control even if their title is held by different business entities.

rules.title: Rentals under 1 year stay in the rental company's fleet
rules.plain_english: A machine rented or leased for less than one year belongs to the rental company's fleet for CARB purposes. A lease of one year or more can move the machine into the renter's fleet, but only if the written lease says so.

rules.verbatim_quote: “Rental or Leased Fleets” – Vehicles that are owned by a rental or leasing company and that are leased by the same lessee for a period of one year or more may be excluded from the rental company fleet and included in the fleet of the lessee only if such arrangement is delineated in the written lease agreement. Vehicles that are rented or leased for a period of less than one year must be included in the fleet of the rental or leasing company.

rules.title: Off-road diesel equipment may not idle more than 5 minutes
rules.plain_english: No off-road diesel machine may idle for more than five minutes in a row. Exceptions: waiting in a work queue, safety checks, servicing, idling needed to do the machine's work (such as running a crane), warming up to operating temperature, and idling needed for safe operation. For a rented machine, the renter is responsible, and the rental agreement must say so.

exceptions: work the vehicle was designed for (e.g., crane)
parameters.waiver: Executive Officer may grant a written waiver on justification

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: No vehicle or engines subject to this regulation may idle for more than five consecutive minutes. Idling of a vehicle that is owned by a rental company is the responsibility of the renter or lessee, and the rental agreement shall so indicate. The idling limit does not apply to: 1. idling when queuing, 2. idling to verify that the vehicle is in safe operating condition, 3. idling for testing, servicing, repairing or diagnostic purposes, 4. idling necessary to accomplish work for which the vehicle was designed (such as operating a crane), 5. idling required to bring the machine system to operating temperature, and 6. idling necessary to ensure safe operation of the vehicle.

rules.title: Waiting in line before the workday starts is not 'queuing'
rules.plain_english: The idling exception for queuing covers stop-and-go waiting in a work line when shutting off is not practical. Sitting in line with the engine running before the workday or site opens is not queuing, so the 5-minute limit applies.

rules.verbatim_quote: “Queuing” means the intermittent starting and stopping of a vehicle while the driver, in the normal course of doing business, is waiting to perform work or a service, and when shutting the vehicle engine off would impede the progress of the queue and is not practicable. Queuing does not include the time a driver may wait motionless in line in anticipation of the start of a workday or opening of a location where work or a service will be performed.

rules.title: A small fleet that grows has two years to meet medium or large fleet rules
rules.plain_english: If a small fleet grows into a medium or large fleet, it must meet the bigger fleet's requirements on the compliance date two years after the year it grew. rules.title: Emergency projects: no certificate needed, but keep emergency records
rules.plain_english: For true emergency projects, primes and public agencies do not need the fleet certificates, but must keep records showing the equipment was used only for the emergency: a description, the location, the dates, and the fleet's attestation. Routine maintenance or construction is not an emergency.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate and public works awarding bodies
rules.verbatim_quote: Situations in which prime contractors or public works awarding bodies, as applicable, are contracting for projects that are considered emergency operations, as defined in section 2449(c)(18), are exempt from the requirements in section 2449(i)(1)-(3), but must still retain records verifying vehicles subject to the regulation that are operating on the emergency operations project are actually being operated on the project for emergency operations only. These records must include a description of the emergency, the address or a description of the specific location of the emergency, the dates on which the emergency operations were performed, and an attestation by the fleet that the vehicles are operated on the project for emergency operations only.

rules.title: Truck and Bus rule covers diesel vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.plain_english: CARB's Truck and Bus regulation applies to diesel (and dual-fuel or alternative diesel) trucks and buses with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over 14,000 pounds that run in California, whether owned, leased or rented, and to people selling them.

pickups 19,500 lbs GVWR or less used only for personal use

[...] vehicles that are designated as NOx Exempt, must have permanently affixed or painted labels on the left and right door with the letters “NE” in three inch white block letters on a five inch by eight inch black background, unless the owner chooses to comply by using a vehicle location tracking system.
rules.notes: CARB NOx Exempt Area Extensions fact sheet (last updated June 27, 2019).

rules.title: Truck and Bus records: give to CARB within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: Truck fleet owners must keep the required records and give them to CARB within five business days of a request.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.verbatim_quote: The owner shall provide these records to an agent or employee of the ARB within five business days upon request.

rules.title: Truck and Bus violations: civil or criminal penalties
rules.plain_english: Failing to comply, failing to report, or filing false statements under the Truck and Bus rule can bring civil or criminal penalties under Health and Safety Code sections 39674 and following.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person who fails to comply with the general requirements of this regulation, who fails to submit any information, report, or statement required by this regulation, or who knowingly submits any false statement or representation in any application, report, statement, or other document filed, maintained, or used for the purposes of compliance with this regulation may be subject to civil or criminal penalties under sections 39674, 39675, 42400, 42400.1, 42400.2, 42402.2, and 43016, of the Health and Safety Code.
rules.notes: Statutory dollar amounts not read (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: DMV will not register a noncompliant diesel truck over 14,000 lb
rules.plain_english: Under SB 1 (2017), the DMV checks Truck and Bus compliance at registration and refuses to register noncompliant diesel vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)

rules.title: Clean Truck Check covers all non-gasoline vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.plain_english: California's Clean Truck Check (heavy-duty inspection and maintenance) program applies to every non-gasoline heavy-duty vehicle (over 14,000 lb GVWR) operating in California and its owner and operator, plus freight contractors and brokers who hire them. Zero-emission vehicles, authorized emergency vehicles and military tactical vehicles are excluded.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: All non-gasoline heavy-duty vehicles operating in California and the owners and operators of such vehicles. [...] “Heavy-duty vehicle” means any motor vehicle having a manufacturer's GVWR greater than 14,000 pounds.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). Unverified: search excerpts (trade press) report that on January 27, 2026 EPA disapproved applying the program to out-of-state trucks.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check compliance: fee paid, vehicle reported, passing test, no open citations or recalls
rules.plain_english: CARB deems a heavy-duty vehicle compliant (within 72 hours) only when the owner has paid the annual compliance fee, reported owner and vehicle information, submitted a passing emissions test, and has no outstanding enforcement actions or emissions/OBD recalls on the vehicle.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: The Executive Officer shall deem a vehicle compliant within 72 hours with the HD I/M Regulation upon finding all the following conditions are met: [...] (2) The owner has reported to CARB the owner and vehicle information required under section 2197.2(b). (3) The owner has demonstrated compliance with the periodic vehicle emission testing requirements by submitting a passing compliance test as specified in section 2196.2. (4) The owner has no outstanding enforcement actions on the vehicle in question. (5) The owner has no outstanding emissions or OBD-related recalls on the vehicle in question.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check tests: twice a year at first, then 4 times a year for OBD trucks
rules.plain_english: Most heavy-duty vehicles must pass an emissions test twice per compliance year during the first three years of periodic testing. Three years after periodic testing took effect, trucks with on-board diagnostics (OBD) move to four tests a year. Motor homes and agricultural vehicles test once a year.

parameters.quarterly_start: 3 years after the effective date of 13 CCR 2196.2 (see air-ctc-periodic-testing-start)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Motor homes registered in California and agricultural vehicles shall be subject to an annual compliance deadline. (2) For the first three years of periodic vehicle emission testing requirements specified in section 2196.2, all vehicles other than those specified in (1) shall be subject to semi-annual compliance deadlines. (3) Three years following the effective date of periodic vehicle emission testing requirements specified in section 2196.2, an OBD-equipped vehicle other than those specified in (1) shall be subject to quarterly compliance deadlines.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). If periodic testing took effect October 1, 2024 (CARB fact sheet, not read), quarterly testing for OBD vehicles would start about October 1, 2027; CARB's own announcement of that date was not read.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check periodic testing took effect Oct. 1, 2024; first deadlines Jan. 1, 2025
rules.plain_english: CARB set October 1, 2024 as the start of periodic emissions testing; compliance deadlines from January 1, 2025 on require a passing test.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.citation: 13 CCR 2195(d), 2196.2; CARB Clean Truck Check overview fact sheet
rules.notes: Unverifiable from primary text: the regulation (2195(d)) leaves the date to a Notice Register/website notice (no earlier than January 1, 2024), and CARB's Clean Truck Check fact-sheet pages (HTML) returned a rate-limit page. Dates come from search-result excerpts of CARB's overview fact sheet and FAQ.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check deadlines follow the DMV registration date
rules.plain_english: For California-registered trucks the compliance year runs from the DMV registration expiration date. Twice-a-year deadlines fall on that day in months 6 and 12; quarterly deadlines in months 3, 6, 9 and 12.

parameters.compliance_year_anchor: DMV registration expiration day and month (CA-registered)
parameters.short_month_rule: last day of month if the day does not exist
parameters.non_ca_registered: based on last digit of VIN

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Semiannual deadlines occur on a vehicle’s compliance year expiration day in months six and twelve of each compliance year with the deadline in month twelve being the final day of a vehicle’s compliance year. [...] Quarterly deadlines occur on a vehicle’s compliance year expiration day in months three, six, nine, and twelve of each compliance year [...] For California-registered vehicles, the start and end date of every compliance year shall align with the day and month of a vehicle’s DMV [...] registration expiration date.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: A Clean Truck Check test within 90 days before a deadline counts to the next deadline
rules.plain_english: If you pass the test within 90 days before your upcoming deadline, the truck is compliant through the following deadline. Testing more than 90 days early only covers you up to the upcoming deadline.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: If a vehicle owner demonstrates vehicle compliance within 90 calendar days or less of the vehicle’s immediate upcoming compliance deadline, the Executive Officer shall deem a vehicle compliant with the HD I/M Regulation up to the vehicle’s subsequent compliance deadline as long as the additional conditions specified in section 2196.1(b) are met.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check annual compliance fee: $30 base, adjusted yearly for inflation
rules.plain_english: Each registered heavy-duty vehicle owes CARB an annual compliance fee before its first compliance for the year. The regulation set it at $30.00 and CARB adjusts it each year by the California Consumer Price Index, publishing the new amount by July 1.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: The Executive Officer shall assess a compliance fee of $30.00 to the vehicle owner for each registered vehicle prior to the first demonstration of compliance for a vehicle in a given compliance year. The Executive Officer shall adjust the compliance fee annually based on the California Consumer Price Index (CCPI) as updated by the Department of Industrial Relations and shall publish the adjusted compliance fee by July 1st of each year on CARB’s website.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). Search excerpts of CARB's fee pages report $31.18 for 2025 and $32.13 for deadlines on and after January 1, 2026, with a 2027 update page; those pages could not be read, so the current amount is left null.

rules.title: DMV registration requires Clean Truck Check compliance within 90 days before renewal
rules.plain_english: CARB tells the DMV a heavy-duty vehicle is compliant for registration only if all compliance conditions were met within 90 days before the registration date. Without it, registration can be held.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: The Executive Officer shall notify the DMV a vehicle has been deemed compliant by CARB with the HD I/M Regulation for registration purposes if compliance with section 2196.1(b)(1) through (b)(5) has been demonstrated for the vehicle within 90 calendar days in advance of the registration date.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Buying a used heavy truck: compliance must be within the last 90 days; new trucks 30 days
rules.plain_english: When a heavy-duty vehicle changes owner or registration in California, the new owner must make sure compliance was demonstrated within the 90 days before the transfer. A buyer of a brand-new vehicle has 30 days after purchase to report and pay (no test needed).
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Upon a transfer of ownership or registration in California, the new owner shall demonstrate compliance by ensuring the requirements of section 2196.1(b)(1) through (b)(5) have been met for the vehicle within the last 90 calendar days in advance of the transfer date. [...] (2) Upon transfer of ownership of a new motor vehicle as defined in Health and Safety Code section 39042 to an ultimate purchaser, the new owner shall demonstrate compliance within 30 calendar days of the vehicle purchase
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Hiring heavy trucks: only use Clean Truck Check-compliant vehicles and keep proof 5 years
rules.plain_english: Anyone (other than a broker) who contracts for heavy-duty vehicles to operate in California, such as a contractor hiring haul trucks, must use only compliant vehicles or fleets, and keep for each hired truck either a copy of its compliance certificate valid at dispatch or the fleet's Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance dated within 12 months. Keep records 5 years and produce them within 72 hours.

proof_options: HD I/M compliance certificate valid at time of dispatch
Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance dated within 12 months, obtained before contract

rules.applies_to: Freight contractors: any person, other than a broker, who contracts for heavy-duty vehicles to operate in California (including construction firms hiring trucking)
rules.verbatim_quote: Any freight contractor shall only contract with compliant vehicles or fleets and comply with the recordkeeping requirements specified in section 2197.3(b). [...] (A) A copy of the vehicle’s HD I/M compliance certificate, valid at the time of dispatch, for each vehicle dispatched to, from, or within California; or (B) An Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance for the fleet dispatching vehicles to California to which the vehicle belongs. [...] 2. Dated within 12 months of the date the vehicle is contracted by the freight contractor.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). 'Freight contractor' means 'any person, excluding a broker, who enters into a contract with any party requiring the operation of a heavy-duty vehicle within California.' Section 2197 took effect on a date CARB announced (no earlier than July 1, 2023 per 2195(d)); that date was not read.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check records: keep 5 years, produce within 72 hours
rules.plain_english: Unless a section says otherwise, records required by Clean Truck Check must be kept at least five years and given to CARB staff, inspectors or police within 72 hours of a written or verbal request.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California; freight contractors and brokers
rules.verbatim_quote: Unless otherwise specified, affected entities shall retain the specified records for a minimum of five years from date of entry, and shall provide them to CARB staff, inspectors, or peace officers within 72 hours of official written or oral request.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check Five-Day Pass: once a year per vehicle, apply 7 business days ahead
rules.plain_english: An owner bringing a noncompliant heavy truck into California for a short job can ask CARB for a Five-Day Pass to operate up to five consecutive days. It is available once per calendar year per vehicle; apply at least seven business days before entry and keep the pass in the truck.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Prior to operating in California, a vehicle owner may obtain written approval from the Executive Officer to operate a vehicle for up to five consecutive calendar days without being subject to the requirements of section 2196(a)(1) and (a)(2). [...] Vehicle owners are eligible to apply for a Five-Day Pass prior to travelling to California once per calendar year per vehicle. The vehicle owner shall submit an application for a Five-Day Pass to the Executive Officer at least seven business days prior to the vehicle’s planned travel or entry in California
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Do not operate heavy trucks with tampered or defective emission controls
rules.plain_english: Owners may not run a heavy-duty vehicle in California with tampered or defective emission control parts, improperly installed aftermarket parts, or (for 1974 and newer) without meeting the emission standards on its legible emission label.

prohibited: tampered or defective emission control components
1974+ vehicle not meeting federal standards per legible emission control label

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Not operate any vehicle in California with tampered or defective emission control components.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check violations: penalties under the Health and Safety Code
rules.plain_english: Violating Clean Truck Check, misreporting, or filing false statements can bring penalties under Health and Safety Code Division 26, Parts 2 and 5. Blaming the driver, owner or freight contractor does not reduce the penalty.

parameters.statutes: Health and Safety Code Division 26, Parts 2 and 5

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California; freight contractors and brokers
rules.verbatim_quote: may be subject to penalties under Health and Safety Code, Division 26, Parts 2 and 5. Evidence of fault on the part of the registered owner, vehicle operator, freight contractor, or other entity shall not be considered a mitigating circumstance for assessing penalties.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). Dollar amounts not read (leginfo blocked); search excerpts mention up to $10,000 per day, unverified.

rules.title: Advanced Clean Fleets (as of Sept. 10, 2026) covers only state and local government fleets
rules.plain_english: CARB's amended Advanced Clean Fleets regulation, effective September 10, 2026, applies to state and local government agencies' vehicles over 8,500 lb GVWR (and to anyone hiring those fleets). It no longer contains zero-emission purchase rules for private contractors' truck fleets.

parameters.covered_fleets: state or local government agencies with jurisdiction in California

rules.applies_to: Private construction fleets (status check) and public agencies operating vehicles over 8,500 lb GVWR
rules.verbatim_quote: Unofficial electronic version of the Advanced Clean Fleets regulation, effective September 10, 2026 [...] This article applies to any state or local government agency with jurisdiction in California that owns, leases, rents, contracts for the operation of, or operates one or more vehicles specified in section 2013(a)(2) in California on or after September 10, 2026. This article does not apply to federal fleets.
rules.notes: CARB's unofficial version of the Final Regulation Order approved by OAL September 10, 2026; it contains only Article 3.2 (state and local government fleets) and Article 8 (2049, hiring compliant fleets). Private fleets remain subject to Truck and Bus and Clean Truck Check.

rules.title: Diesel trucks over 10,000 lb may not idle more than 5 minutes
rules.plain_english: No diesel commercial vehicle over 10,000 lb GVWR may idle more than five minutes in a row anywhere in California, and a diesel auxiliary power unit may not run more than five minutes within 100 feet of homes, schools, hospitals and similar places. This binds owners, drivers and the companies that dispatch them.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.verbatim_quote: diesel-fueled commercial motor vehicles that operate in the State of California with gross vehicle weight ratings of greater than 10,000 pounds that are or must be licensed for operation on highways. [...] 1. No vehicle subject to this section shall idle for more than 5 consecutive minutes at any location. 2. No diesel-fueled APS subject to this section shall be operated for greater than 5 minutes at any location when within 100 feet of a restricted area.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: Truck idling exception: power take-off work such as mixers, cranes and pumps
rules.plain_english: The 5-minute truck idling limit does not apply while the engine powers a PTO for the work the truck is built for, such as a crane, pump, drill, hoist, lift or ready-mix concrete drum. Other exceptions include traffic, queuing more than 100 feet from homes or schools, safety inspections, servicing, and adverse weather or breakdowns.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.verbatim_quote: (D) idling when the vehicle is queuing that at all times is beyond 100 feet from any restricted area; [...] (H) idling when positioning or providing a power source for equipment or operations, other than transporting passengers or propulsion, which involve a power take off or equivalent mechanism and is powered by the primary diesel engine for: 1. controlling cargo temperature, operating a lift, crane, pump, drill, hoist, mixer (such as a ready mix concrete truck), or other auxiliary equipment;
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: Truck idling 'restricted area': property with homes, schools, hotels, hospitals or care facilities
rules.plain_english: A restricted area is any property zoned for houses or apartments, schools, hotels, motels, hospitals, senior care or child care that has at least one such unit. Near these (within 100 feet) even queuing and clean-idle trucks may not idle over 5 minutes.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.verbatim_quote: “Restricted area” means any real property zoned for individual or multifamily housing units, schools, hotels, motels, hospitals, senior care facilities or child care facilities, that has one or more of such units on it.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: Illegal truck idling fine: up to $1,000 per day for owner and driver
rules.plain_english: Air districts, CARB and any law enforcement agency can fine both the owner and the driver of a truck of 10,000 lb or more up to $1,000 per day for illegal idling.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.verbatim_quote: Any law enforcement department, including air districts and CARB, can fine a 10,000 pound or greater truck owner and driver up to $1000 per day for illegal idling (13 CCR 2480 & 2485).
rules.notes: CARB fact sheet (October 2021). 2485(g) cites HSC 39674 et seq. for violations on or after January 1, 2015.

rules.title: Motor carriers must give dispatched drivers their contact details
rules.plain_english: A company that dispatches a diesel truck over 10,000 lb must give the driver the carrier's business name, address, contact person and phone. On request, the driver must show an enforcement officer their license, the vehicle registration and that carrier information.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.verbatim_quote: On or after January 1, 2015, a motor carrier that dispatches a vehicle subject to the requirements of this section must provide the following information to a dispatched driver: 1. motor carrier's business name 2. motor carrier's street address, state, zip code; 3. motor carrier contact person's name; and 4. motor carrier contact person's business phone number.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: PERP registration is voluntary, but air district permits are mandatory
rules.plain_english: CARB's Portable Equipment Registration Program lets portable equipment such as compressors, generators, concrete pumps, drill rigs and crushers operate statewide without a permit from each of the 35 air districts. Registering is voluntary; if a district requires a permit, you must get it even if the unit is in PERP.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: The Portable Equipment Registration Program (PERP) is a voluntary statewide program to register portable equipment such as air compressors, generators, concrete pumps, tub grinders, woodchippers, water pumps, drill rigs, pile drivers, rock drills, abrasive blasters, aggregate screening and crushing plants, and concrete batch plants. [...] If a district decides something needs a district permit, the owner/operator must obtain the district permit to use it, even if it is registered in PERP.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. CARB's off-road booklet: 'If you own or operate a portable auxiliary engine 50 hp or greater, you may need a permit or registration to legally operate in California.'

rules.title: Portable means it does not stay at one location more than 12 months
rules.plain_english: Equipment counts as portable (eligible for PERP instead of a stationary permit) only if it can be moved, is not on a foundation, and does not stay at the same location more than 12 consecutive months. The clock starts when it arrives, not when it first runs, and moving it away and back to reset the clock is not allowed.

parameters.clock_starts: when first brought onto the location

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: It does not reside at the same location for more than 12 consecutive months. [...] The 12-month time period starts when the equipment is first brought onto the location.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: PERP registration lasts 3 years; send the renewal at least 2 months before expiry
rules.plain_english: A PERP registration usually expires 3 years from the month issued. CARB emails a renewal invoice about 120 days before expiration; return it to PERPrenewals@arb.ca.gov at least 2 months before expiration to avoid late fees. Older-tier engines may get shorter terms.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: You will receive a renewal invoice approximately 120 days before the expiration date. This renewal invoice must be completed and emailed to PERPrenewals@arb.ca.gov at least 2 months prior to expiration to avoid any late renewal fee penalties. [...] In most cases, the registration expires 3 years from the month it was originally issued.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: PERP fees: $805 per engine, $490 per equipment unit (renewal $735 / $420)
rules.plain_english: Registering a portable engine or pile driver in PERP costs $805 (with placard); an equipment unit costs $490. Renewal is $735 per engine and $420 per equipment unit, plus a penalty fee if late. Fees are not refundable.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: Initial registration: 1. Engine or pile driver: $805 [...] 2. Equipment unit: $490 [...] Renewal registration: 1. Engine or pile driver: $735 [...] 2. Equipment unit: $420
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. Fee amounts as listed in the September 29, 2026 FAQ. Multiple-engine (4+) inspection discount needs a letter of intent to the home district within 45 days of initial registration or by January 30 for renewals.

rules.title: PERP projects over 2,500 bhp in extreme ozone areas: notify the district 14 days ahead
rules.plain_english: If an onshore project in an extreme ozone nonattainment district will have registered portable engines totaling more than 2,500 bhp on site at once, the person responsible must notify the district in writing at least 14 days before startup, or within 72 hours if the total goes over 2,500 bhp after startup. Projects using only Tier 4 engines in remote locations are excused.

parameters.applies_in: districts designated extreme non-attainment for ozone (e.g., South Coast, San Joaquin Valley)
parameters.exempt: only Interim Tier 4/Tier 4 Final engines at locations > 1/2 mile from schools, businesses, hospitals, residences, daycare

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: if an onshore project commences operation in a district designated as extreme non-attainment for ozone and the total maximum rated horsepower of registered engines located simultaneously on the project site exceeds 2,500 brake horsepower (bhp), the person responsible for the project must notify the district in writing at least 14 days prior to startup. If the project exceeds 2,500 bhp after startup, the district must be notified within 72 hours of the exceedance.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. The district list for 'extreme' ozone nonattainment is not given in the FAQ.

rules.title: PERP diesel engine eligibility: Tier 4 Final (or flex) only
rules.plain_english: New PERP registrations for diesel engines are limited to current-tier engines: 50-750 bhp must be Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex or Tier 3 flex; over 750 bhp must be Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex or Tier 2 flex. Tier 3 hazardous-location engines stay eligible until January 1, 2029.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: 2. Engines rated at 50 bhp to 750 bhp, certified to the following federal emission tier levels: • Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex, or Tier 3 flex. 3. Engines rated over 750 bhp, certified to the following federal emission tier levels: • Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex, or Tier 2 flex.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: Portable diesel engines 50 bhp and up must meet CARB's Portable Engine ATCM
rules.plain_english: Most portable diesel engines rated 50 bhp or more must meet CARB's Portable Engine Airborne Toxic Control Measure, whether they are PERP-registered, district-permitted or unpermitted. Engines under 50 bhp and engines that propel vehicles are not covered.

not_subject: engines that propel vehicles or mobile equipment

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: Most portable diesel engines rated 50 bhp or greater are subject to the Portable Engine ATCM. It does not matter if the engine is registered in PERP, permitted with a local air district, or unpermitted.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: Portable engine fleets: small 750 bhp or less, large over 750 bhp
rules.plain_english: For the Portable Engine ATCM, a fleet with 750 total bhp or less is small and must follow the tier phase-out schedule; over 750 bhp is large. All companies registering since June 30, 2019 are small fleets.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: Large fleets have a total maximum horsepower over 750 bhp and follow either the tier phase out schedule or the fleet average compliance option. [...] Small fleets have a total maximum horsepower of 750 bhp or less. [...] Small fleets must follow the tier phase out schedule.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. Engine-specific phase-out dates are printed on each engine's registration certificate (93116.3(c)(1)).

rules.title: Low-use portable engines: 200 hours a year; annual report by March 1
rules.plain_english: A low-use portable engine may run no more than 200 hours per calendar year (hours outside California or in emergencies do not count), must have a non-resettable hour meter, and its annual low-use report is due March 1 for the prior year.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: May not operate more than 200 hours per calendar year. [...] Annual low-use reports must be submitted by March 1 of each year for operation the prior year as required by section 93116.4(d)(1) of the Portable Engine ATCM.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: PERP renewal needs an hour meter reading taken within 12 months of expiration
rules.plain_english: To renew a registered portable diesel engine, enter the hour meter reading and the date taken on the renewal invoice; the reading must be within 12 months of the registration's expiration date.

parameters.applies_to: registered diesel engines (not spark-ignition, two-engine cranes, sweepers, water well rigs)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.verbatim_quote: The owner must also list the date the reading was taken, and the reading must be within 12 months of the registration’s expiration date.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: South Coast: no visible dust beyond the property line
rules.plain_english: In the South Coast AQMD, no person may let dust from a construction site, storage pile or disturbed ground stay visible in the air past the property line, or exceed 20% opacity from vehicle movement.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall cause or allow the emissions of fugitive dust from any active operation, open storage pile, or disturbed surface area such that: [...] (A) the dust remains visible in the atmosphere beyond the property line of the emission source; or (B) the dust emission exceeds 20 percent opacity (as determined by the appropriate test method included in the Rule 403 Implementation Handbook), if the dust emission is the result of movement of a motorized vehicle.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Does not apply when wind gusts exceed 25 mph if Table 3 contingency measures are used and records kept (403(g)(2)(A)).

rules.title: South Coast: use the Rule 403 Table 1 best available control measures
rules.plain_english: Every active construction operation in the South Coast AQMD must use the applicable best available control measures from Rule 403 Table 1 for each dust source: backfilling, clearing and grubbing, cut and fill, demolition, disturbed soil, earth-moving, hauling bulk materials, staging areas, stockpiles, traffic areas, trenching, truck loading, unpaved roads and others.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall conduct active operations without utilizing the applicable best available control measures included in Table 1 of this Rule to minimize fugitive dust emissions from each fugitive dust source type within the active operation.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Category 'required_document' is used because the measures are a required checklist; no plan filing is required below the large-operation threshold.

rules.title: South Coast: downwind PM10 may not exceed upwind by more than 50 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: If dust is sampled, the PM10 level downwind of a site may not be more than 50 micrograms per cubic meter above the upwind level.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall cause or allow PM10 levels to exceed 50 micrograms per cubic meter when determined, by simultaneous sampling, as the difference between upwind and downwind samples collected on high-volume particulate matter samplers or other U.S. EPA-approved equivalent method for PM10 monitoring.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Large operations that routinely use Table 2 measures and keep records are exempt from (d)(3) (403(g)(5)); if SCAQMD monitors, Rule 304.1 fees may apply (403(h)).

rules.title: South Coast: track-out under 25 feet and cleaned up every workday
rules.plain_english: Mud and dirt tracked onto paved roads may not extend 25 feet or more from the site exit, and all track-out must be removed at the end of each workday or evening shift.

parameters.cleanup: end of each workday or evening shift

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall allow track-out to extend 25 feet or more in cumulative length from the point of origin from an active operation. Notwithstanding the preceding, all track-out from an active operation shall be removed at the conclusion of each workday or evening shift.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast: sites of 5+ acres or 100+ cy/day need a track-out control at each exit
rules.plain_english: A site with 5 or more acres disturbed, or importing/exporting 100 cubic yards or more of material a day, must have at least one track-out control at every exit to a paved public road: a washed-gravel pad (1-inch rock, 6 inches deep, 30 ft wide by 50 ft long), 100 ft by 20 ft of paving, a 24 by 10 ft wheel shaker, a wheel washer, or an approved equivalent.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall conduct an active operation with a disturbed surface area of five or more acres, or with a daily import or export of 100 cubic yards or more of bulk material without utilizing at least one of the measures listed in subparagraphs (d)(5)(A) through (d)(5)(E) at each vehicle egress from the site to a paved public road. (A) Install a pad consisting of washed gravel (minimum-size: one inch) maintained in a clean condition to a depth of at least six inches and extending at least 30 feet wide and at least 50 feet long. [...] (B) Pave the surface extending at least 100 feet and at least 20 feet wide. (C) Utilize a wheel shaker/wheel spreading device consisting of raised dividers (rails, pipe, or grates) at least 24 feet long and 10 feet wide to remove bulk material from tires and vehicle undercarriages before vehicles exit the site.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast 'large operation': 50+ acres disturbed or 5,000 cy/day three times a year
rules.plain_english: A large operation is any site with 50 or more acres of disturbed surface, or earth-moving of 3,850 cubic meters (5,000 cubic yards) or more in a day on three days within the last 365 days. Large operations have extra notice, records, signs and supervisor duties.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (21) LARGE OPERATIONS means any active operations on property which contains 50 or more acres of disturbed surface area; or any earth-moving operation with a daily earth-moving or throughput volume of 3,850 cubic [...] meters (5,000 cubic yards) or more three times during the most recent 365-day period.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: file Form 403 N within 7 days of qualifying
rules.plain_english: Once a site becomes a large operation, submit a signed Large Operation Notification (Form 403 N) to SCAQMD within 7 days, with the responsible people's names, addresses and phones, a description of the work and a site map.

contents: names, addresses, phone numbers of responsible persons

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) submit a fully executed Large Operation Notification (Form 403 N) to the Executive Officer within 7 days of qualifying as a large operation; (B) include, as part of the notification, the name(s), address(es), and phone number(s) of the person(s) responsible for the submittal, and a description of the operation(s), including a map depicting the location of the site;
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: daily dust-control records kept 3 years
rules.plain_english: Large operations must keep daily records of the dust control actions taken, keep them at least three years, and show them to SCAQMD on request.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (C) maintain daily records to document the specific dust control actions taken, maintain such records for a period of not less than three years; and make such records available to the Executive Officer upon request;
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: post project contact signs before earthmoving
rules.plain_english: Before any earthmoving on a large operation, install project signs with contact information meeting the Rule 403 Implementation Handbook standards.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (D) install and maintain project signage with project contact signage that meets the minimum standards of the Rule 403 Implementation Handbook, prior to initiating any earthmoving activities;
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). The Implementation Handbook (sign size and content) was not read.

rules.title: South Coast large operations: certified dust control supervisor on call within 30 minutes
rules.plain_english: Large operations must name a dust control supervisor employed or hired by the owner or developer, on site or able to be there within 30 minutes during working hours, with authority to order dust controls, who has completed SCAQMD's Fugitive Dust Control Class.

parameters.training: AQMD Fugitive Dust Control Class certificate
parameters.employer: property owner or developer (employee or contractor)

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (E) identify a dust control supervisor that: (i) is employed by or contracted with the property owner or developer; (ii) is on the site or available on-site within 30 minutes during working hours; (iii) has the authority to expeditiously employ sufficient dust mitigation measures to ensure compliance with all Rule requirements; (iv) has completed the AQMD Fugitive Dust Control Class and has been issued a valid Certificate of Completion for the class; and
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast: tell SCAQMD within 30 days after a site stops being a large operation
rules.plain_english: Notify SCAQMD in writing within 30 days after the site no longer qualifies as a large operation.

parameters.trigger: site no longer qualifies as a large operation

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (F) notify the Executive Officer in writing within 30 days after the site no longer qualifies as a large operation as defined by paragraph (c)(18).
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). The rule's cross-reference '(c)(18)' is as printed; large operations are defined in (c)(21).

rules.title: South Coast: Form 403 N valid 1 year; resubmit 30 days before it expires
rules.plain_english: An accepted Large Operation Notification is valid one year. Resubmit it at least 30 days before expiration or it lapses; if nothing changed, a short no-change statement (Form 403NC) is enough.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: Any Large Operation Notification submitted to the Executive Officer or AQMD-approved dust control plan shall be valid for a period of one year from the date of written acceptance by the Executive Officer. [...] must be resubmitted annually by the person who conducts or authorizes the conducting of a large operation, at least 30 days prior to the expiration date, or the submittal shall no longer be valid as of the expiration date.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast high winds: gusts over 25 mph trigger Table 3 contingency measures
rules.plain_english: When wind gusts exceed 25 mph, the visible-dust and PM10 limits are excused only if the Table 3 contingency measures are carried out for each dust source and daily records are kept. Contingency options include stopping earth-moving or watering soil within 15 minutes before moving it, and watering disturbed areas 3 to 4 times a day.

earth_moving: water soil not more than 15 minutes before moving

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: The provisions of paragraphs (d)(1) and (d)(3) shall not apply: (A) When wind gusts exceed 25 miles per hour, provided that: [...] (i) The required Table 3 contingency measures in this Rule are implemented for each applicable fugitive dust source type, and; (ii) records are maintained in accordance with subparagraph (e)(1)(C).
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: 12% soil moisture checks and watering unpaved roads every 2 hours
rules.plain_english: Large operations must follow Table 2: keep earth-moving soil at 12% moisture or more, checking twice in the first three hours and twice every four hours after; water unpaved roads at least every two hours (3 times per 8-hour day), or once a day with a 15 mph limit, or use a chemical stabilizer.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: Maintain soil moisture content at a minimum of 12 percent, as determined by ASTM method [...] Two soil moisture evaluations must be conducted during the first three hours of active operations during a calendar day, and two such evaluations each subsequent four-hour period of active operations; [...] Water all roads used for any vehicular traffic at least once per every two hours of active operations [3 times per normal 8 hour work day]; OR [...] Water all roads used for any vehicular traffic once daily and restrict vehicle speeds to 15 miles per hour; OR
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Earth-moving more than 100 ft from all property lines may instead be watered to keep visible dust under 100 ft in any direction (1a-1).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: stabilize completed grading within 5 working days
rules.plain_english: On large operations, completed grading areas must get chemical stabilizer within five working days of finishing grading, or be treated like inactive areas (watering, or vegetative cover started within 21 days).

parameters.vegetation_density: less than 30% unstabilized ground within 90 days of planting

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (2c) Apply chemical stabilizers within five working days of grading completion; OR [...] Establish a vegetative ground cover within 21 days after active operations have ceased.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast: stockpiles near occupied buildings max 8 ft; keep 6 inches of freeboard on haul trucks
rules.plain_english: Under Table 1, stockpiles within 100 yards of occupied off-site buildings may be no higher than 8 feet unless a water-truck road or full irrigation system reaches the top, and haul trucks must keep at least six inches of freeboard (per Vehicle Code 23114).
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: Maintain at least six inches of freeboard on haul vehicles; and [...] Stockpiles within 100 yards of off-site occupied [...] buildings must not be greater than eight feet in [...] height; or must have a road bladed to the top to allow [...] water truck access or must have an operational water irrigation system that is capable of complete stockpile coverage.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Table 1 guidance also suggests limiting staging-area vehicle speeds to 15 mph.

rules.title: South Coast: a contractor's Rule 403 duty ends with its contract (grading: 5 days after final inspection)
rules.plain_english: A contractor is no longer covered by Rule 403 after its contract ends if it used the required controls during the contract. A grading contractor's coverage for a phase ends after that phase, provided controls were kept up through five days after the final grading inspection.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.verbatim_quote: (H) Any contractor subsequent to the time the contract ends, provided that such contractor implemented the required control measures during the contractual period. (I) Any grading contractor, for a phase of active operations, subsequent to the contractual completion of that phase of earth-moving activities, provided that the required control measures have been implemented during the entire phase of earth-moving activities, through and including five days after the final grading inspection.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: Coachella Valley: dust control plan approved before earthmoving over 5,000 sq ft
rules.plain_english: In the Coachella Valley, any project disturbing more than 5,000 square feet may not start earthmoving until SCAQMD approves a fugitive dust control plan. SCAQMD acts within 30 days; plans last one year and must be resubmitted at least 30 days before expiry. Keep the plan on site, post contact signs, and for 50+ acres name a dust control supervisor.
rules.applies_to: Construction and earthmoving in the Coachella Valley portion of the South Coast AQMD
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person who conducts or authorizes the conducting of an active operation with a disturbed surface area of more than 5,000 square feet shall not initiate any earth-moving activities unless a fugitive dust control plan is prepared and approved by the Executive Officer in accordance with the requirements of subdivision (f) and the Rule 403.1 Implementation Handbook. [...] Any fugitive dust control plan approved by the Executive Officer shall be valid for a period of one year from the date of approval. Any approved fugitive dust control plan must be resubmitted annually, at least 30 days prior to the expiration date, or the fugitive dust control plan shall expire as of the expiration date.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403.1 as amended April 2, 2004. Exempt where a city/county has a District-approved dust control ordinance (403.1(i)(4)).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: Dust Control Plan before work on 10+ acres residential, 5+ acres non-residential, or >2,500 cy/day
rules.plain_english: In the San Joaquin Valley, submit a Dust Control Plan before starting any construction on a site with 10 or more acres disturbed (residential), 5 or more acres (commercial, industrial, institutional, public), or moving more than 2,500 cubic yards a day of material on at least three days. Work may not begin until the District approves it, and you must give written notice within 10 days before earthmoving starts.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: An owner/operator shall submit a Dust Control Plan to the APCO prior to the start of any construction activity on any site that will include 10 acres or more of disturbed surface area for residential developments, or 5 acres or more of disturbed surface area for non-residential development, or will include moving, depositing, or relocating more than 2,500 cubic yards per day of bulk materials on at least three days. Construction activities shall not commence until the APCO has approved or conditionally approved the Dust Control Plan. An owner/operator shall provide written notification to the APCO within 10 days prior to the commencement of earthmoving activities via fax or mail.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: District decides on a Dust Control Plan within 30 days (submit 30 days ahead)
rules.plain_english: The District approves, disapproves or conditions a Dust Control Plan within 30 days of submittal; a plan with no District comments after 30 days is automatically approved. The District's guidance is to submit at least 30 days before construction starts. One plan can cover several sites starting within 12 months.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: The APCO shall approve, disapprove, or conditionally approve the Dust Control Plan within 30 days of plan submittal. A Dust Control Plan is deemed automatically approved if, after 30 days following receipt by the District, the District does not provide any comments to the owner/operator regarding the Dust Control Plan.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page). SJVAPCD's 2024 dust control brochure: 'Plans must be submitted to the District at least 30 days prior to commencing construction.'

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: 48-hour notice for 1-10 acre residential and 1-5 acre non-residential sites
rules.plain_english: Smaller construction sites that do not need a full Dust Control Plan still need written notice to the District at least 48 hours before earthmoving: residential sites from 1 to under 10 acres, non-residential sites from 1 to under 5 acres.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: On residential development construction sites ranging from 1.0 to less than 10.0 acres in area, an owner/operator shall provide written notification to the District at least 48 hours prior to his/her intent to commence any earthmoving activities. [...] On non-residential development construction sites ranging from 1.0 to less than 5.0 acres in area, an owner/operator shall provide written notification to the District at least 48 hours prior to his/her intent to commence any earthmoving activities.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: keep the approved Dust Control Plan on site; one person must take District dust training
rules.plain_english: Keep a copy of the approved Dust Control Plan at the project site; it stays valid until all dust-generating work ends, and breaking it is a rule violation. At least one key person for the owner/operator, or whoever prepares the plan, must complete the District's Dust Control Training Class.

parameters.plan_valid_until: termination of all dust generating activities

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: An owner/operator shall retain a copy of an approved Dust Control Plan at the project site. The approved Dust Control Plan shall remain valid until the termination of all dust generating activities. [...] At least one key individual representing the owner/operator or any person who prepares a Dust Control Plan must complete a Dust Control Training Class conducted by the District.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: limit visible dust to 20% opacity on construction sites
rules.plain_english: All construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the Valley must use enough controls (pre-watering, phasing, watering or stabilizers during work, wind barriers, stabilizing haul roads) to keep visible dust emissions at or below 20% opacity and keep surfaces stabilized.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall perform any construction, demolition, excavation, extraction, or other earthmoving activities unless the appropriate requirements in sections 5.1 through 5.5 are sufficiently implemented to limit VDE to 20% opacity and comply with the conditions for a stabilized surface area when applicable.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: stabilize 0.5+ acre areas left unused 7 days or more
rules.plain_english: Any disturbed area of half an acre or more that sits unused for seven or more days must be stabilized (watered, treated, or access restricted) to meet the District's stabilized-surface conditions.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: If an area having 0.5 acres or more of disturbed surface area remains unused for seven or more days, the area must comply with the conditions for a stabilized surface area as defined in section 3.58 of Rule 8011.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: 15 mph on uncontrolled unpaved haul roads, with signs every 500 feet
rules.plain_english: On construction sites, keep vehicles to 15 mph on uncontrolled unpaved access and haul roads, and post DOT-standard speed limit signs at each entrance and at least every 500 feet, readable both directions.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: An owner/operator shall limit the speed of vehicles traveling on uncontrolled unpaved access/haul roads within construction sites to a maximum of 15 miles per hour. [...] At a minimum, speed limit signs shall also be posted at least every 500 feet and shall be readable in both directions of travel along uncontrolled unpaved access/haul roads.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: stop soil-disturbing work when wind dust exceeds 20% opacity
rules.plain_english: Whenever visible dust exceeds 20% opacity, stop outdoor construction and earthmoving that disturbs soil (indoor trades may continue), and keep water trucks running unless unsafe.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Cease outdoor construction, excavation, extraction, and other earthmoving activities that disturb the soil whenever VDE exceeds 20% opacity. [...] Continue operation of water trucks/devices when outdoor construction excavation, extraction, and other earthmoving activities cease, unless unsafe to do so.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley demolition: water unpaved surfaces within 100 ft within 1 hour
rules.plain_english: When razing buildings, keep visible dust under 20% opacity and apply water within one hour of demolition to unpaved surfaces within 100 feet of the demolished structure.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Apply water within 1 hour of demolition to unpaved surfaces within 100 feet of the demolished structure.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: Rule 8021 exemptions for small additions and remodels
rules.plain_english: Rule 8021 does not apply to maintenance or remodeling of existing buildings and additions that increase building area by no more than 50% or 10,000 sq ft (whichever is less), all additions to existing single-family homes, or fire-prevention disking under half an acre. Track-out from these jobs must still be cleaned up under Rule 8041.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Maintenance or remodeling of existing buildings and additions to existing buildings where total building area is not increased by more than fifty percent, or 10,000 square feet, whichever is less; but not including ancillary construction such as expanding parking lots. [...] All additions to existing single family residential buildings.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley Dust Control Plan fee: $493 (from July 1, 2026); $102 to modify
rules.plain_english: Filing a Rule 8021 Dust Control Plan costs a nonrefundable $493 (effective July 1, 2026), covering any administrative changes. A modification of an approved plan costs $102. Fees unpaid 60 days after submittal incur late charges.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Every person filing a Dust Control Plan subject to the provisions of Rule 8021, Section 6.3.1, shall pay to the District, upon filing, the nonrefundable fee of $493. [...] Any person submitting a request to modify an existing approved Dust Control Plan, shall pay to the District, a fee of $102.
