rules.notes: SJVAPCD Rule 3135 as amended May 15, 2025, effective July 1, 2026. Search excerpts show the prior fee was $456 (version effective July 1, 2025); not used.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: remove all visible track-out at the end of each workday; no blowers or dry brooms
rules.plain_english: Remove all visible carryout and track-out from paved public roads at the end of every workday. Leaf blowers and dry rotary brushes or brooms may not be used to clean it up; use manual sweeping, a wetted rotary broom, a PM10-efficient sweeper, or flushing where allowed.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: The use of blower devices, or dry rotary brushes or brooms, for removal of carryout and trackout on public roads is expressly prohibited. [...] Owners/operators shall remove all visible carryout and trackout at the end of each workday.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: track-out reaching 50 feet must be removed immediately
rules.plain_english: In urban areas (inside city limits or unincorporated islands surrounded by a city), and on rural construction projects of 10 acres or more, prevent track-out or remove it immediately once it extends 50 feet or more from the site exit.

parameters.urban_area: incorporated city or unincorporated area completely surrounded by a city

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Within urban areas, an owner/operator shall prevent carryout and trackout, or immediately remove carryout and trackout when it extends 50 feet or more from the nearest unpaved surface exit point of a site. [...] Within rural areas, construction projects 10 acres or more in size, an owner/operator shall prevent carryout and trackout, or immediately remove carryout and trackout when it extends 50 feet or more from the nearest unpaved surface exit point of a site.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: track-out device needed at 150 trips/day, 20 heavy-truck trips/day, or Dust Control Plan sites
rules.plain_english: A site with 150 or more vehicle trips a day, or 20 or more trips a day by vehicles with 3+ axles, or any site under a Dust Control Plan, must install a track-out control device at every exit to a paved public road; if track-out still occurs, it must be removed within half an hour.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: An owner/operator of any site with 150 or more vehicle trips per day, or 20 or more vehicle trips per day by vehicles with three or more axles shall take the actions for carryout and trackout as specified in Section 5.8. [...] In the event that measures specified in Section 5.8.1 are insufficient to prevent carryout and trackout, removal of any carryout and trackout must be accomplished within one-half hour of the generation of such carryout and trackout.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley track-out devices: grizzlies 25 ft, gravel pad 50 ft x 3 in deep, or 100 ft of paving
rules.plain_english: An acceptable track-out device is a grizzly or similar rumble device at least 25 feet long across the full exit width, a gravel pad of 1-inch or larger rock at least 3 inches deep and 50 feet long across the full width (clean gravel off the road at least every 24 hours), or paving at least 100 feet long across the full width.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: For use of grizzlies or other similar devices designed to removed dirt/mud from tires, the devices shall extend from the intersection with the public paved road surface for a distance of at least 25 feet, and cover the full width of the unpaved exit surface for at least 25 feet. [...] For use of gravel pads, coverage with gravel shall be at least one inch or larger in diameter and at least 3 inches deep, shall extend from the intersection with the public paved road surface for a distance of at least 50 feet, and cover the full width of the unpaved exit surface for at least 50 feet.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page). Paving option (5.9.3): at least 100 feet, full width.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: daily dust-control records kept 1 year after the project ends
rules.plain_english: For each day a dust control measure is used, record the measure, where and how much area was covered, and the date, amount and frequency of any dust suppressant (with the product sheet). Keep records one year after the project ends (five years for Title V sources) and show them to the District on request.

contents: date, amount and frequency of suppressant

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Such records shall include the type of control measure(s) used, the location and extent of coverage, and the date, amount, and frequency of application of dust suppressant, manufacturer’s dust suppressant product information sheet that identifies the name of the dust suppressant and application instructions. Records shall be kept for one year following project completion that results in the termination of all dust generating activities.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley APCD counties
rules.plain_english: SJVAPCD covers San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings and Tulare counties and the Valley air basin portion of Kern County. Regulation VIII dust rules apply to projects in these areas.

parameters.partial: Kern (San Joaquin Valley Air Basin portion)

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Serving San Joaquin, Stanislaus and Merced counties [...] Serving Madera, Fresno and Kings counties [...] Serving Tulare and Valley air basin portions of Kern counties
rules.notes: From SJVAPCD's official 2024 fugitive dust control brochure.

rules.title: Bay Area CEQA basic dust measures: water twice a day, cover haul trucks, 15 mph, stop work over 20 mph wind
rules.plain_english: Bay Area projects are expected to use all nine basic dust measures: water exposed surfaces twice daily; cover haul trucks; remove track-out daily with wet power vacuum sweepers (no dry power sweeping); 15 mph on unpaved roads; pave and lay pads as soon as possible; suspend excavation, grading and demolition when average wind exceeds 20 mph; wash trucks and equipment before leaving; treat unpaved access roads 100+ ft from pavement with 6-12 inches of wood chips, mulch or gravel; and post a dust complaint sign with a contact who responds within 48 hours.

sign_must_show: lead agency contact name and phone

rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.citation: BAAQMD CEQA Guidelines (2022) Table 5-2, BMPs B-1 to B-9
rules.verbatim_quote: All exposed surfaces (e.g., parking areas, staging areas, soil piles, graded areas, and unpaved access roads) shall be watered two times per day. [...] All haul trucks transporting soil, sand, or other loose material off-site shall be covered. [...] All vehicle speeds on unpaved roads shall be limited to 15 mph. [...] All excavation, grading, and/or demolition activities shall be suspended when average wind speeds [...] exceed 20 mph. [...] This person shall respond and take corrective action within 48 hours.
rules.notes: BAAQMD 2022 CEQA Guidelines, Chapter 5, Table 5-2. The Guidelines are nonbinding advice to CEQA lead agencies, but a project must implement all basic BMPs for construction dust to be found less than significant, so lead agencies commonly impose them as mitigation conditions. The 2022 Guidelines supersede the 2017 version; the exact adoption date was not read.

rules.title: Bay Area CEQA enhanced dust measures near sensitive uses
rules.plain_english: Near schools, homes or other sensitive uses, the Bay Area AQMD strongly encourages enhanced measures: limit simultaneous ground disturbance, wind breaks of at most 50% porosity, early ground cover, sandbags on slopes over 1%, minimal stockpiles, and hydroseed or stabilize areas inactive for 10 or more calendar days.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.citation: BAAQMD CEQA Guidelines (2022) Table 5-3, BMPs E-1 to E-6
rules.verbatim_quote: Hydroseed or apply non-toxic soil stabilizers to construction areas, including previously graded areas, that are inactive for at least 10 calendar days.
rules.notes: BAAQMD 2022 CEQA Guidelines, Chapter 5, Table 5-2. The Guidelines are nonbinding advice to CEQA lead agencies, but a project must implement all basic BMPs for construction dust to be found less than significant, so lead agencies commonly impose them as mitigation conditions.

rules.title: Bay Area trackout rule applies to construction sites over 1 acre
rules.plain_english: Bay Area AQMD Rule 6-6 covers large construction, bulk material and disturbed surface sites, meaning sites where the construction, material handling and disturbed area totals more than 1 acre.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: This Rule does not apply to Bulk Material Sites, Construction Sites and Disturbed Surface Sites less than 1 acre. [...] Large Construction Site: Any Construction Site where the total land area covered by construction activities, bulk material handling operations and disturbed surfaces is greater than 1 acre.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Bay Area: clean up track-out over 25 feet within 4 hours; no more than 1 quart left at day's end
rules.plain_english: At each active exit, track-out on the paved public road that exceeds a cumulative 25 linear feet and raises visible dust must be cleaned up within 4 hours of noticing it, and no more than 1 quart of track-out may remain on the road at the end of the workday.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: The owner/operator of any Large Bulk Material Site, Large Construction Site, or Large Disturbed Surface Site shall not cause or allow trackout at any active exit from such site onto an adjacent paved public roadway or shoulder of a paved public roadway that exceeds cumulative 25 linear feet and creates fugitive dust visible emissions without cleaning up such trackout within 4 hours of when the owner/operator identifies such excessive trackout; and shall not cause or allow more than 1 quart of trackout to remain on the adjacent paved public roadway or the paved shoulder of the paved public roadway at the end of any workday.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Bay Area: track-out cleanup may not raise dust over 20% opacity for more than 3 minutes an hour
rules.plain_english: Cleaning up track-out may not create visible dust over 20% opacity (Ringelmann No. 1) for more than 3 minutes in any 60-minute period.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: shall not cause or allow a fugitive dust visible emission during cleanup of any trackout that exceeds 20 percent opacity as determined by EPA Method 203B (or as dark in shade as that designated as Number 1 on the Ringelmann Chart), for a period or aggregate periods of more than 3 minutes in any 60-minute period.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Bay Area: check each exit for track-out twice a workday and keep logs 2 years
rules.plain_english: Large sites that produce track-out must check each active exit at least twice every workday at peak exit times, log which exits were checked, log every time track-out exceeded 25 feet and the cleanup done, and keep the records two years for the District.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.verbatim_quote: Monitor the extent of the trackout at each active exit from the site onto a paved public road at least twice during each workday, at times when vehicle traffic exiting the site is most likely to create an accumulation of trackout, or as otherwise specified by the APCO; [...] Maintain the records required by Sections 6-6-501.2 and 501.3 for two years, in electronic, paper hard copy or log book format, and make them available to the APCO upon request.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).
